title: Premiere Pro for Beginners: Project Setup, Timeline Editing, Color, Audio, Subtitles — Hands-on Walkthrough
summary: This YouTube tutorial by Gavin Herman is a structured, beginner-focused Premiere Pro course. It guides viewers from setting up a project (folder structure, preferences, and performance choices) through creating a first edit, adding narration and sound design, performing basic color correction and grading with LUTs and Lumetri, adding captions, and applying motion graphics and keyframing. The video emphasizes real-world exercises, practical keyboard shortcuts, and iterative refinements (transitions, text, shapes, and audio). It also demonstrates an end-to-end export workflow and introduces techniques such as stabilization, nesting, and caption-to-graphics workflows, with occasional notes on AI-assisted subtitling and auto-transcription features.
topics: Premiere Pro interface and workspaces
Project folder structure (media and project files)
Drive selection for performance (SSD vs HDD)
Auto-save and cache management
Memory (RAM) allocation for editing workflows
Sequence settings: frame rate, resolution, and color space
Importing media and creating a sequence
Timeline basics: snapping, unlinking video and audio, and ripple delete
Clip trimming with playhead and ripple edits
Using the slip tool for precise timing
Applying and adjusting transitions (cross dissolve) and default transition via Shift+D
Text and essential graphics: creating, centering, and font choices
Animating text and converting captions to graphics
Using shapes and nesting for organized motion graphics
Ultra Key for green screen and keying cleanup
Warp Stabilizer for stabilization
Color correction and LUTs (C-Log 3 to Rec. 709) with Lumetri Color
Lumetri scopes and IRE range; exposure, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, and saturation
Color matching with comparison view and Apply Match
Audio mixing basics: essential sound panel, track mixer, denoise, dynamics, and gain
Ducking, mastering, and amplitude/compression adjustments
Subtitles and captions from transcript; caption styling and animation
Keyframing and motion graphics (Transform, position, scale, rotation) with easing
Exporting: in/out points, 1080p H.264, and final render
